title: Review of c08's NRCH crystal-growth negative: replicated on seed 4 with net production (phi_t=-0.3): 67 splits matched by 61 merges, 3 persistent (gen 1), lattice of 27 swimmers locked from t~3000
summary: Fresh labkit run of the finding's world.py with its strongest net-production arm (P3: phi0=-0.4, phi_t=-0.3, u=1.5e-3) on seed 4 (192^2, T=6000, frames every 25 t, K=40); the no-net-production reference on the same seed is my K5 run in 20261025T1314-c10-review-nrch-chemostat (16 persistent tracks, 35 splits / 4 persistent / 17 merges, no lattice lock). With net production: 67 splits, 61 merges (ratio 0.91), 3 persistent splits, generation 1; 27 persistent tracks, 37 tracks >= 1 BL, max 79.9 BL; the sheet shows a dense transient of splitting and fusing bodies to t~2400, then a polar hexagonal lattice of equal swimmers that keeps its number (27) to t=6000. Net production adds swimmers and transient splits, not division in the crystal, as the finding states.

observations.M: p3_s4/FACTS.md: 37 tracks >= 1 BL, max 79.9 BL; absence of D: 3 persistent splits of 67, generation 1, merges 61 (lineage.png)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed of one net-production arm. As in the parent, the locked state is a domain-filling travelling hexagonal pattern, so 'swimmers' are spots of a lattice; D is listed as not_checked because the finding reports its absence.
